_comment: Two interpolation surfaces live in this file. (1) Generator-time: tokens like Infrastructure Manager are uppercase-snake-case placeholders replaced by `template-manager generate` before the scenario is built — they appear as literal display values at runtime. (2) Runtime: tokens like {{count}} are i18next interpolation, replaced by `t(key, { count })` at render time. Keys that start with an underscore (like this one) are sentinels — skipped by the codegen, parity test, and unused-key audit.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Substrate condition at a glance, and what the instrument cannot see about this machine.
dashboard.sourceUnavailable: A board source did not answer. Every figure here is computed over the sources that did.
dashboard.confidenceNote: Every figure above is computed only over the sources that answered. Where a source did not answer, its cells are absent from the numerator and from the denominator alike, so this board understates rather than invents.
dashboard.findingsNote: The highest-ranked findings the cascade returned. The focus page carries the full surface and the rule that ranked each one.
dashboard.findingsEmptyBody: Every readable source answered and none returned a ranked finding. That is an empty surface, not an unread one, and it is not a passing grade.
dashboard.findingsUnavailableBody: The finding sources could not be read, so nothing is ranked. No claim is made about what the plant is doing.
dashboard.sourcesNote: Every source this board read, with the reason verbatim where one did not answer. An unreachable source is a fact about the instrument; none of its cells is presented as in band.
dashboard.sourcesEmptyBody: Neither response named its sources, so this board cannot say how much of the surface it read. It does not assume it read all of it.
dashboard.instrumentNote: The API this board reads. It reports the instrument's own liveness, never the plant's.

designLanguage.title: Instrument language
designLanguage.description: Every primitive of the annunciator language, in every state it can be in. This page exists so the language can be reviewed in one view, and so a regression in it is visible before a real surface consumes it.
designLanguage.plateNote: A plate's tag is a real reference — a substrate cell id, a rung tag, or a device address. A section with no real reference to carry renders no tag.
designLanguage.lampNote: Eight states, and the length of that list is the point. Colour is supplementary in every one: each lamp also carries a distinct mark and a text label, so the panel stays readable when colour is removed.
designLanguage.ringNote: Five arcs, one per ladder rung, in dependency order from twelve o'clock. The ring exists so the shape of a device's coverage reads before any label does.
designLanguage.statNote: A figure that could not be computed renders an em dash, never a zero. On this surface a fabricated zero is the specific dishonesty the instrument exists to remove.
designLanguage.gridNote: Rows are devices, columns are the five rungs, cells are lamps. A real table with two header axes, because a screen reader must be able to announce the finding.
designLanguage.blindNote: The differentiator. A dark region is not empty and is not “no data” — it is a dated measurement meaning nobody is watching this, and here is how long that has been true.
designLanguage.fixtureCaption: Fixture data. These rows are fixed sample values chosen to exercise every state, not a reading of this host.
designLanguage.statNotComputable: Not computable — renders an em dash, never a zero

substrate.title: The machine
substrate.description: Every device attached to this host, and which rungs of the observability ladder are covered for each. The dark regions are the content: they mean nobody is watching, and they carry the date that became true.
substrate.sourceUnavailable: A substrate source did not answer. The instrument names the failure rather than fabricating a reading.
substrate.unavailableBody: The device graph could not be read, so this board has nothing to show. That is a fact about the instrument, not about the machine — no coverage figure is implied and none is printed.
substrate.noDevicesBody: The source answered and reported no devices in this class. That is different from the source being unreachable, and both are different from the machine having nothing attached.
substrate.constellationNote: Each class orbits the host on a real parent edge, carrying a five-segment ring — one arc per ladder rung. A class with no lit arc is drawn as a dashed outline: the device tree declares it, and nothing watches it.
substrate.matrixNote: Rows are devices, columns are the five rungs. Select a class in the constellation to filter; select a row to drill into one device.
substrate.matrixCaption: {{count}} devices graded against an owner-authored denominator with {{confidence}} confidence. {{rationale}}
substrate.noRemediation: No remediation is declared for this gap yet.
substrate.blindForDays: Longest-standing blindness on this device: {{days}} days.
substrate.portabilityNote: How much of the capability surface is actually proven, per operating system. Amber means qualified on real hardware of that platform. Build-verified means it compiles and passes fixtures and has never run on a real host — a different fact, shown differently.
substrate.portabilityCaption: {{count}} capabilities resolved against the closed platform-status vocabulary. A status outside that vocabulary fails a repository gate rather than being silently downgraded.

coverage.title: What is actually instrumented?
coverage.description: Every coverage space this instrument grades, the ratio it computes, and the confidence of the owner-authored denominator that ratio was measured against. A space that could not be read is named as unread — it is never counted as a gap and never printed as zero.
coverage.sourceUnavailable: A coverage source did not answer. The instrument names the failure rather than fabricating a ratio.
coverage.unavailableBody: The coverage source could not be read, so this page has no ratio to show. That is a fact about the instrument, not about the plant — no cell is reported missing and no ratio is implied.
coverage.chromeNote: Which declared spaces answered at read time. This is instrument state and it is kept out of the plant figures below, so an owner outage can never read as a coverage collapse.
coverage.chromeAllRead: Every declared space answered at read time.
coverage.gridNote: One panel per space. The ratio, its denominator confidence and the rationale for that confidence are one visual unit: this instrument never prints a ratio the reader cannot qualify.
coverage.projectionUnavailable: This space could not be read. Its cells keep their authored status; none is counted as missing and no ratio is implied.
coverage.confidenceNote: Each ratio above already carries this qualifier beside it. The table restates every space's denominator claim in full, because a rationale that only appears in a tooltip is a rationale nobody reads.
coverage.confidenceCaption: {{read}} of {{total}} declared spaces answered. A space that did not answer states its failure reason in place of a rationale.
coverage.openLoopNote: Every MISSING cell, oldest gap first, with the date the gap was declared and how long it has stood. A gap carrying no date is the thing this instrument exists to prevent, so it is shown as undated rather than as a zero-day gap.
coverage.openLoopCaption: {{missing}} missing cells of {{total}} cells the coverage source returned.
coverage.openLoopEmptyBody: The cell source answered and reported no MISSING cells. That is different from the source being unreadable, and both are different from the space being fully instrumented.
coverage.openLoopUnavailable: Open-loop cells could not be read because the cell source failed. No gap count is implied.
coverage.integrityNote: Findings raised while parsing the setpoint itself. These are faults in the instrument's own definition of the plant, so they are stated ahead of any figure computed from it.
coverage.integrityEmptyBody: The setpoint parsed and raised no findings. That is the instrument reporting on itself; it says nothing about the plant.
coverage.integrityUnavailable: The setpoint could not be validated because the coverage source failed. No cell count is shown.

condition.title: Can the reading be believed?
condition.description: Every reading in this space, the verdict on whether it can be trusted, and — only where trust holds — the band it fell in. A reading the instrument cannot trust is never given a band, because banding an untrusted number is how a dashboard learns to lie.
condition.sourceUnavailable: A condition source did not answer. Its readings are named unavailable rather than inferred healthy.
condition.unavailableBody: The live condition source could not be read. No healthy reading is inferred, and no aggregate is shown.
condition.trustNote: The verdict distribution, the checked denominator and the total are one figure. Split apart, they would let a reader quote a count without the population it was drawn from.
condition.readingsNote: One row per reading. Trust is graded first and the band verdict is withheld wherever trust does not hold, so an unverified number can never be presented as in band.
condition.readingsCaption: {{shown}} readings returned, {{trusted}} of them trusted. Only the trusted rows carry a band verdict.
condition.valueUnavailable: No value was returned by this source.
condition.untrustedNotBanded: Not banded — trust must hold before a band means anything.
condition.emptyTitle: Nothing is instrumented in this space
condition.emptyBody: The condition source answered and returned no readings. An empty space is not a passing space: no aggregate is computed and nothing here is reported as in band.
condition.sourcesNote: An unreachable source is a fact about the instrument, not about the plant. It is named here with its reason verbatim, and the readings it cost are marked unavailable rather than quietly dropped.
condition.noSourceReportBody: The condition response did not include source availability, so the instrument cannot say which sources answered. It does not assume they all did.
condition.historyEmptyTitle: Select a cell to inspect history
condition.historyEmptyBody: Historical readings are re-banded against the current deadband when a cell is selected, never replayed against whatever verdict was stored at the time.

focus.title: What should happen next?
focus.description: The findings this instrument would read first, in cascade order, each carrying the rule that put it where it is. This surface is read-only: the scenario holds no actuation right and offers no control that changes the plant.
focus.sourceUnavailable: A finding source did not answer. What is ranked below is ranked over the sources that did.
focus.rationaleBody: Findings are ordered by the reliability cascade: instrument integrity is read before plant condition, so a trust finding outranks a band finding drawn from the same sensor. Rank is the cascade's output, not a severity guess, and it is stated on every row.
focus.rankedNote: Each finding names the stage that ranked it and the sensor that would prove it closed.
focus.unavailableBody: The instrument could not read its finding sources, so nothing is ranked. An unread source is not an empty surface.
focus.nothingReadBody: No finding source answered, so the instrument has nothing to rank. This is not the same as having no findings.
focus.emptyBody: {{read}} of {{total}} finding sources answered and none returned a ranked finding. Every source was read, so this is an empty surface rather than an unread one.
focus.unranked: The cascade returned no rank for this finding.
focus.sourcesNote: How much of the error surface was actually read. A source that did not answer is named with its reason, so an empty ranking can be told from an unread one.
focus.sourcesEmptyBody: The focus response did not name its sources, so the instrument cannot say how much of the error surface it read.
focus.efficacyEmptyBody: A finding's named sensor is re-read only after downstream work records a completion. Until then there is nothing to grade, and nothing is graded as passing.

health.title: API Health
health.error: Unable to reach the API. Make sure the scenario is running through `vrooli scenario start`.

errorBoundary.message: An unexpected error occurred while rendering the page. Try again, or reload if the problem persists.
